_note: Owner's decision 2026-11-12: the picture family is chosen by what the client does, not at random. First matching group wins (most keyword hits; ties go to the earlier group). The first preview takes the first family of the group that exists in the library for the client's tone; the second and third previews take the next ones, always three different families. Aurora is not in the library (rejected). 2026-11-18 (owner: many more variants for the kinds of apps, and a rule for which goes where): groups that name a subject stand first — court, field, writing, documents, building, data, money — and lead with photographs of that subject (media/library/<family>, two tones, natural colours); the four broad groups after them are the fall-back. A family ending in 2 is the same subject in other photographs, so three designs of one client show three pictures of its own subject. A subject group needs two telling words (`min`): one word alone (book a call, a match for you) does not set a client among stadiums or paper — it falls to the broad groups.
